page: Google Cloud Platform a3-highgpu-2g is an accelerator-optimized server configured with two NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs providing a total of 159 GB of VRAM. The host system features 52 vCPUs powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8481C processors running at 2.7 GHz, built on the x86_64 architecture with 26 physical cores. System memory totals 468.0 GB, yielding 9.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided via 1608 GB of NVMe SSD.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier performance in LLM inference workloads. For a small 135M model, prompt processing reaches 10254.62 tokens per second and text generation reaches 350.02 tokens per second. For a medium 7B model, prompt processing achieves 5644.37 tokens per second and text generation reaches 194.27 tokens per second. CPU-bound benchmarks show strong performance, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 17415.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 54314.03. Memory bandwidth is also strong, measuring 3828.33 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 214.57 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads.

From a resource density perspective, the server pairs high-end accelerator hardware with substantial memory and dedicated CPU resources, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that can fully utilize both the GPUs and the high-bandwidth memory. However, the lack of complimentary public IPv4 addresses and the absence of benchmark data for large 70B LLM models represent notable constraints. This server configuration is suited for medium-scale LLM inference, machine learning training, database operations, and high-throughput data processing.
